description: Argument categories for claim extraction and judging. Each claim is tagged with one or more categories. Adding a new category here automatically updates the extraction and judge prompts — no code change needed.

categories.name: accountability
categories.description: High-stakes ownership of outcomes — figuring out the work, executing, reporting back, being the person responsible for whether it works. Not just building something but owning whether it was right.

categories.name: stakeholder_fluency
categories.description: Translating across the technical/non-technical boundary — requirements gathering, training non-technical staff, turning vague direction into something buildable. The axis is technical/non-technical boundary crossing.

categories.name: technical_ownership
categories.description: Owned specific systems end-to-end — built it, maintained it, accountable for its correctness in production. Named system, named employer, full lifecycle.

categories.name: autonomy
categories.description: Operated independently under high expectations — figured out the path without being told how, did the job without someone defining it first. Solo operation under real accountability.

categories.name: technical_depth
categories.description: Deep knowledge of specific tools, domains, or problem spaces — not just used the tool but understood its failure modes, tradeoffs, and how to get reliable output from it.

categories.name: approach_method
categories.description: How this person consistently thinks and works — a cross-cutting professional method provable across employers. Not what was built but how the person approaches any problem of this type.
anchor_signals: before writing a line of code

categories.name: disposition
categories.description: Who they are as an engineer — professional character, what they bring that is rare or specific to them. Not a skill claim but an assertion about who this person is, provable by pattern across their work.

categories.name: motivation
categories.description: What draws them to this kind of work and why — specific orientation toward the work, not generic enthusiasm. What kind of problem they find meaningful and what they get from solving it.

categories.name: communication
categories.description: Making things visible, legible, and documented — proactively surfacing constraints, writing documentation others rely on, making complex things clear across any audience. The axis is clarity and proactive information sharing.

categories.name: leadership
categories.description: Directing work, setting priorities, making architectural calls with authority, owning a project or initiative beyond individual contribution. Distinct from autonomy — this is directing others, not just operating independently.
